rationale: Start with a broad gradient to maximize the chance of observing all 10 compounds while mapping retention and critical separations. The midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how much of the current resolution margin survives. Keeping composition endpoints and temperature fixed makes the gradient-slope effect easier to interpret.

Test temperature-driven selectivity at the faster gradient to separate the critical middle cluster without restoring the time penalty. A substantial temperature change will reveal whether this is a promising route toward full resolution.

Combine an intermediate high temperature with a slightly shallower gradient to balance separation of the middle cluster against the new close pair seen at 60 C. This should retain a short analysis time while improving the weakest separations.

Preserve the optimal gradient slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute and the same temperature, but end the gradient earlier. All peaks previously eluted before this new gradient endpoint, so this distinct method should retain the maximum CRF.

Maintain the maximum-scoring gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint further. The gradient still extends beyond the last observed peak, so the separation and CRF should remain unchanged.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; test a slightly shallower gradient to seek a larger resolution margin for the two closest pairs. The modest increase in retention may still preserve a zero time penalty.

Test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to shorten retention while retaining the gradient slope used in injection 7. Since the maximum CRF is already established, this explores whether an equally scoring method offers a better resolution margin or shorter runtime.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope from injection 8 to improve the 1.29-resolution pair while retaining the higher starting organic fraction. This may restore CRF 1.000 with both critical pairs above 1.5 and the last peak still near eight minutes.

Pair a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to build on injection 9’s balanced critical separations. This tests another potentially maximum-scoring method with a larger minimum-resolution margin while targeting last-peak elution near eight minutes.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a 5 C decrease from injection 4 to assess temperature sensitivity of its two marginally resolved pairs. This isolates temperature while keeping the established optimal gradient unchanged.

With the maximum CRF already secured, explore a lower-temperature selectivity regime rather than further adjusting the narrow 55 C optimum. The fast gradient tests whether reordered middle peaks can achieve full resolution without a time penalty.

Return to the successful 55 C regime and slightly flatten injection 9’s gradient to improve its limiting resolution of 1.55. This tests whether a larger separation margin is possible while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty boundary.

The maximum CRF is already secured; explore whether higher starting organic and 60 C move the close middle pair past its selectivity crossover. This could reveal a faster, fully resolved alternative rather than another equivalent gradient.

Increase starting organic another step to test whether the critical middle pair continues separating beyond its crossover. Injection 14 leaves some resolution margin between the early peaks, potentially allowing a faster maximum-scoring method.

Return to the starting composition of injection 14 to preserve early-peak separation, but steepen the gradient to test selectivity of the critical middle pair. This explores a shorter maximum-scoring alternative while the established CRF 1.000 method remains available.

Use a gradient slope between injections 9 and 13 to balance their two critical separations while keeping the last peak below eight minutes. This targets the established maximum CRF with a slightly larger minimum-resolution margin than injection 9.

Reduce injection 10’s gradient slope from 0.055 to 0.050 to improve its limiting middle-pair resolution while retaining the stronger separation of the other critical pair. Injection 17 shows that elution beyond eight minutes can still incur no time penalty, leaving room for this adjustment.

Slightly flatten injection 18’s gradient to raise its limiting resolution from 1.41 toward baseline separation. The other critical pair has margin, so this may yield another CRF 1.000 method if the longer retention remains within the zero-penalty window.

Preserve injection 4’s gradient slope through the first nine peaks, then use a lower-organic hold to elute the final compound. This tests whether the maximum CRF can be maintained with a lower endpoint despite some delay of the last peak.

Preserve injection 13’s gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint to 0.60. Its last peak eluted before this shortened gradient would end at the outlet, so this method should retain CRF 1.000 and the observed minimum resolution of 1.58.

Slightly flatten injection 19’s gradient to seek a larger minimum-resolution margin than 1.57. The maximum CRF is already secured; this run tests whether improved separation outweighs any time penalty near the nine-minute last-peak boundary.

Test a shorter gradient with nearly the same slope as injection 22, which achieved CRF 1.000 and a minimum resolution of 1.70. The endpoint should remain high enough for all peaks to elute during the gradient, preserving nearly the same separation with slightly shorter retention.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 22 to check the resolution margin around its balanced critical pairs. This should keep both resolutions near 1.70 while testing whether the modest retention increase preserves CRF 1.000.

The maximum CRF of 1.000 is already secured. Use the final injection to test temperature sensitivity of injection 23’s well-resolved, lower-endpoint method by changing only temperature, providing a direct check of the 55 C operating point.
